solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Resign from stage, depressed

parts.note: a step is a stage in a process
feeling down means depressed

explanation.surface: An actor quits the stage, feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a post or office voluntarily is to stand aside from it, a common phrasal verb for quitting.

clue.text: Performing well most of a single carol

indicators.note: most of the word means all but its final letter is kept

parts.note: a single item is one
a carol is a song

explanation.surface: A choir is doing nicely with most of one Christmas carol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims ONE (from 'a single') to ON.
explanation.definitionFit: British idiom for being in top form, like a singer hitting every note.

clue.text: Oustanding rift Eric mended

indicators.note: something mended has been put back together, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A quarrel with Eric has been patched up splendidly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oustanding' is a typo in the printed clue for 'Outstanding'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something superb or excellent is outstanding.

clue.text: Sew harness

definitions.meaning: to stitch loosely with long temporary stitches
riding gear such as saddle and bridle for a horse

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: basting with long stitches, and the equestrian word for saddlery.

clue.text: Blame sales person over fish

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
the roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A salesman is blamed for something to do with fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to censure or rebuke someone is to find fault with them.

clue.text: One books stage performance that's perfect

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books
an act is a turn on stage

explanation.surface: Someone reserves a show that turns out flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something whole and undamaged is perfect, unbroken in every part.

clue.text: Where Newport is: a US State

parts.note: Newport is the county town of the Isle of Wight, abbreviated IOW

explanation.surface: A quiz question asks which American state has a town called Newport.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Wight is an island off southern England; Newport is its main town. 'Newport' tempts toward Rhode Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this Midwestern farming state is one of the fifty in the union.

clue.text: Ollie's partner's recited a piece of poetry

indicators.note: recited means spoken out, so the letters come from how the words are said

parts.note: Oliver Hardy's comedy partner was Stan Laurel, so this is Stan's

explanation.surface: Stan Laurel recites a bit of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurel and Hardy were a classic comedy double act; 'Stan's a' said out loud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A verse grouping of lines in a poem is a section of the whole.

clue.text: African city a clinic a pet-owner's got inside

indicators.note: the city is tucked within the run of letters of these words

explanation.surface: A pet owner attends a vet's clinic in a South African city.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the legislative capital of South Africa, on the Cape peninsula.

clue.text: Counterpart rings around very quietly

indicators.note: the rings go around the next piece

parts.note: two rings are two O shapes
pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quietly

explanation.surface: A colleague phones round in a hushed voice.
explanation.walkthrough: This is British slang for one's colleague or opposite number.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal term for one's equivalent or partner on the other side or in the same role.

clue.text: Old Roman Catholic: an ogre

explanation.surface: An elderly Catholic is called a monster.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantasy monster of Tolkien and folklore, a brutish humanoid creature.

clue.text: Land in gaol, bizarrely, after a very short time

indicators.note: the scrambled part comes after the short time

parts.note: mo, short for moment, is a very short time

indicators.note: bizarrely means oddly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone ends up oddly imprisoned after only a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land' looks like a verb but is the definition; 'bizarrely' signals the rearrangement, and 'after' places it behind the short time.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an Asian country between Russia and China is a nation, or land.

clue.text: Re-enlist eccentric fan of radio show

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A quirky radio fan signs up for the army again.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tunes in to and follows a radio programme is one of its audience.

clue.text: Sort of train from east, however, going west

indicators.note: in an across entry, going west means read right to left

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
but means however

explanation.surface: A train heads west though it came from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: The London Underground is popularly called this.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an underground railway train in London.

clue.text: One-storey home to place casually on a base

parts.note: to bung is British slang for to toss or put casually
base can mean low or mean

explanation.surface: A single-level house set down casually on a foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a house built all on the ground floor, with no upstairs.

clue.text: Speed of boat a problem

definitions.meaning: a nautical mile per hour, the unit of a ship's speed

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a nautical unit of speed and a tangled difficulty.

clue.text: To upset cat is a gamble

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: puss is a cat

explanation.surface: Annoying a cat is a risky move.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an even chance, decided as if by flipping a coin.

clue.text: The lanes winding around remote island

indicators.note: winding around suggests twisting, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Country lanes wind their way across a far-flung isle.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a remote South Atlantic outpost, where Napoleon was exiled.

clue.text: Somehow got ale flowing smoothly

indicators.note: somehow signals that these letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Someone managed to get beer flowing nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical term for playing notes in a smooth, connected way.

clue.text: Blooming locusts appearing regularly!

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: Locusts turn up everywhere, curse them!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' looks like a mild curse; it means in flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowers that have opened are said to be in bloom, as in the roses are now in flower.

clue.text: Used to live close to meadow before

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Someone once lived near a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A past form of 'be', so it says that something existed or lived formerly.

clue.text: Block made of carbon and length of wood

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
a log is a length of wood

explanation.surface: A block built from carbon and timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to obstruct or jam a pipe is to block it.

clue.text: Seize rabbit outside run

indicators.note: the chatter word goes outside the next piece

parts.note: in British slang to rabbit is to chatter, as is to gab
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a rabbit outside its burrow run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' seems the animal, but it is British slang for talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to snatch or take hold of something suddenly.

clue.text: For every boy, a line that's private

parts.note: per means for each
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Every boy gets a private message.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: belonging to one individual and not shared.

clue.text: Choice of work: one's in fashion

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the fashion word

parts.note: ton is an old word for fashion or style
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A trendy person chooses their job.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an alternative that may be picked.

clue.text: Pal of Reg organised game

indicators.note: organised means put in order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Reg's friend set up a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a children's game of vaulting over a crouching player.
